written.myAnswer: Chemistry is a vast and complex subject, so dividing it into branches makes it easier to study. It allows scientists to specialize in particular areas, and this focused study supports research and scientific advances.
Reactions involving electrons outside the nucleus are studied in the chemical branches of chemistry; reactions occurring inside the nucleus are studied in nuclear chemistry.
Analytical chemistry deals with separating and identifying the components of a sample and determining their amounts or concentrations.

Organic chemistry studies carbon compounds, including their composition, structure, properties and reactions. Biochemistry studies the chemical substances and vital processes of living organisms, including the biological molecules involved.
(a) Physical chemistry; (b) Biochemistry; (c) Physical chemistry; (d) Environmental chemistry; (e) Inorganic chemistry; (f) Analytical chemistry.

Inorganic chemistry studies elements and compounds that contain little or no carbon. Organic chemistry studies carbon compounds, including hydrocarbons and their derivatives, but generally excludes simple carbon compounds such as carbonates, bicarbonates, oxides and carbides.
